Electric Current Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge through a cross-section of a conductor. If a net charge q passes through a cross-section in time t, the average current is: I = q / t The SI unit of current is the ampere (A). One ampere is a flow of one coulomb of charge per second. Current is a scalar quantity, even though we show its direction with an arrow, because currents add algebraically and do not follow the laws of vector addition. By convention, the direction of current is the direction in which positive charges would move.

items.question: If the resistance of one component in a series circuit is doubled, what effect will this have on the total resistance?

key_points.point: The total resistance in a series circuit increases when one component has its resistance doubled.
The formula for total resistance in a series circuit is additive.
When resistances are added in series, the total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances.
